//: turbo envMode is STRICT by default on this version (verified on the platform repo, turbo 2.5.4): a variable ABSENT from a task's `env` list DOES NOT REACH that task. When a member package starts reading a new variable, add it to the relevant task's `env` here in the same change. Note that `tasks` accepts task objects ONLY — a '//' comment key inside it is a hard parse error, and turbo accepts only the literal '//' top-level comment key (a '//test-env' key is a parse error). tasks.test.env lists every HASNA_TODOS_* variable apps/todos reads (src, scripts and *.test.ts; the tests spawn the built CLI/MCP/server, so those child processes inherit exactly this set). Measured on turbo 2.5.4: `env: []` filters the variable out of the task (the child sees undefined), an explicit entry passes it through, and a wildcard (HASNA_TODOS_*) does too — the list is explicit so a reader sees which variables the member reads. Regenerate it with: grep -rhoE 'HASNA_TODOS_[A-Z0-9_]+' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.json' apps/todos --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist | sort -u
